Vattenfall and Cementa (2018). CemZero - A feasibility study evaluating ways to reach sustainable cement production via the use of electricity. Public version 2.0. Vattenfall AB and Cementa AB (Heidelberg Cement Group), 2018.

Region: Sweden (greenfield 1 Mt clinker/yr plant, Cementa Slite/Gotland case study). Loaded: Sect. 8 economics (reference plant, amine capture with electric boiler, plasma scenario: capex in 2018 EUR, production cost per t CEMENT, capture and avoidance costs, lower-range sensitivity), Sect. 6 conceptual designs (plasma SEC 4.6 and 4.4 MJ/kg clinker, E-DSR 3.3 GJe/t, flow-heater 151.2 MW, plasma gas 3000-5000 degC), Sect. 5 heat-source temperatures (flow heater, resistance elements), and the lime-kiln thermal energy ranges quoted from the BREF. Authors are the companies (no named authors in the public version). NOT loaded: Sect. 7 wind and grid case study (other-values only), Sect. 2-4 cement chemistry background, Sect. 5.1.3 microwaves and induction results (lab, other-values), figure bars (Fig. 31-33 energy and cost breakdown charts; flowsheet MW in Fig. 20-23 are images, only the printed 151.2 MW and 4.6/3.3 totals loaded). Traps: (1) production costs are per t CEMENT (1.35 Mt cement from 1 Mt clinker), not per t clinker; the CO2 figures are per t cement in Table 15 but absolute t/yr over 1 Mt clinker; (2) capex covers the whole cement factory including cement milling and packing, and the plasma scenario excludes alternative-fuel and coal handling; (3) plasma SEC 4.4-4.6 is ELECTRICITY while the reference 3.5 GJ/t is thermal (no heating value stated); (4) Table 14 (plasma production cost) is an image page in the PDF text layer, read from a rendered page; (5) electricity price 40 EUR/MWh (30 in Table 16), fossil-free power assumed so electricity CO2 is zero; (6) the 100% capture case (CO2 in kiln) needs a gas-tight CO2 atmosphere kiln, the air version leaves kiln CO2 uncaptured; (7) the amine scenario uses an electric boiler, so the heat for capture is electricity, not steam from gas. Locator: printed page numbers (PDF page minus 1; the front matter is unnumbered).
